newsitem.title: THAILAND: Stainless steel demand seen recovering by 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: Stainless steel demand seen recovering by 1997/98.

text.p: Global demand for cold-rolled flat stainless steel products is expected to pick up in the next two years as prices edge down, a market analyst said on Monday.

Heinz Pariser of Heinz H Pariser-Alloy Metal & Steel Market Research told a conference that demand for cold-rolled flat products, which represent about two thirds of the total stainless steel market, was expected to grow to 7.9 million tonnes in 1998 from 6.85 million in 1995.

"After the last stainless steel boom came to an end mid-1995, the industry has been going through a de-stocking phase and demand is likely to pick up in 1997/98," he told the International Stainless Steel Conference.
Pariser said the long-term downward price trend is one of the key factors for demand growth and because of dropping prices the mills will be forced to improve efficiency and technology.

Total capacity for the industry was likely to expand to 9.4 million tonnes in 1998 from 8.6 million tonnes in 1996, Pariser said. Capacity utilisation for cold-rolled flat stainless steel products was forecast to increase to 84.4 percent in 1998 but will remain between 81-82 percent in 1996/97, he added.
